library(nlmixr2lib)

# Model and source

```{r model}
mod <- readModelDb("Cao_2026_tacrolimus")
ui <- rxode2::rxode(mod)
```

* Citation: `r ui$reference`
* Description: `r ui$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.2147/DDDT.S623781>

Cao and colleagues built a one-compartment population PK model for oral
tacrolimus from routine trough concentrations in 31 Chinese adults with
membranous nephropathy (MN). Only body weight was retained, through fixed
allometric exponents; none of the laboratory values or the 18 screened
concomitant medications affected clearance. The model was then used in a
Monte Carlo simulation to recommend weight-banded starting doses for adults
(50-100 kg) and, by extrapolation, for children (10-40 kg), aiming for a
trough of 4-10 ng/mL.

# Population

The analysis used 31 adults with MN treated at a single centre (Affiliated
Hospital of Xuzhou Medical University, Jiangsu, China) between May 2022 and
September 2025. Baseline characteristics (Table 1 of the source) were: 22 men
/ 9 women; age mean 49.35 years (SD 11.07), range 30-67; body weight mean
69.65 kg (SD 11.50), median 67.50, range 52-103. Serum albumin averaged
34.05 g/L (range 19.0-44.5), consistent with the hypoalbuminaemia of
nephrotic-range MN. Concomitant medication counts are Table 2.

Every observation is a trough sampled about 30 minutes before the next dose,
assayed by enzyme-multiplied immunoassay (Emit 2000; routine range
2-30 ng/mL). The paper reports no administered doses.

```{r population}
str(ui$population, max.level = 1)
```

# Source trace

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| `lcl` (CL/F at 70 kg) | 9.54 L/h | Table 3 and Equation (6); bootstrap median 9.66 [1.13, 13.75] |
| `lvc` (V/F at 70 kg) | 76.3 L | Table 3 and Equation (7); bootstrap median 78.9 [3.0, 214.0] |
| `lka` (absorption rate constant) | 4.48 1/h, **fixed** | Table 3 "4.48 (fixed)"; Methods, Modeling, citing references 33-34 |
| `e_wt_cl` (allometric exponent, CL/F) | 0.75, **fixed** | Methods, Equation (3), citing Anderson & Holford 2008; Equation (6) |
| `e_wt_vc` (allometric exponent, V/F) | 1, **fixed** | Methods, Equation (3); Equation (7) |
| `etalcl` (IIV on CL/F) | 0.172 as an **SD** (variance 0.172^2) | Table 3 (omega_CL/F); bootstrap median 0.094 [0.003, 0.381]; scale settled below |
| `addSd` (additive residual error) | 2.504 ng/mL | Table 3 (sigma_1, "additive error"); bootstrap median 2.601 [0.010, 3.508] |
| Structural model: 1-compartment, first-order oral absorption | n/a | Methods, Modeling (CL/F, V/F and Ka) |
| IIV form `B_i = TV(B) * exp(eta_i)` | n/a | Methods, Equation (1) |
| Residual form `E_i = G_i + eps_1` | n/a | Methods, Equation (2) |
| Reference weight 70 kg | n/a | Methods, Equation (3) |
| Simulation regimen: total daily dose in two equal doses; target 4-10 ng/mL | n/a | Methods, Simulation |

The seven equations are images in the article; the values above were read
from the typeset equations and cross-checked against Table 3.

# Simulation design

The paper's Methods state that every simulated daily dose (0.01-0.14 mg/kg/day)
"was administered in two equal daily doses", and that trough samples were
taken about 30 minutes before the next dose. The simulation below therefore
gives half the daily dose every 12 h for 14 days and reads the concentration
11.5 h after the 28th dose. The longest elimination half-life in the
simulated weight range (100 kg) is about 6 h, so this is steady state.

Because the model has a single random effect (`etalcl`), the between-subject
distribution is represented by a deterministic lattice of 200 equally spaced
normal quantiles rather than by random draws. Every number in this vignette is
therefore identical on every machine. Because the model is linear, each weight
is solved once at 1 mg/kg/day and the troughs are scaled by the dose.

```{r cohort}
n_lattice <- 200L
omega_sd <- 0.172 # Table 3, read as a standard deviation (see Check 2)
z_grid <- stats::qnorm((seq_len(n_lattice) - 0.5) / n_lattice)

weights <- tibble::tribble(
  ~WT, ~group,
  50, "Adult", 60, "Adult", 70, "Adult", 80, "Adult", 90, "Adult", 100, "Adult",
  10, "Child", 20, "Child", 30, "Child", 40, "Child"
)
doses <- c(0.01, 0.02, 0.04, 0.06, 0.08, 0.10, 0.12, 0.14) # mg/kg/day

make_events <- function(wt, w_index, eta) {
  ids <- (w_index - 1L) * n_lattice + seq_len(n_lattice)
  dose <- tibble::tibble(
    id = ids, time = 0, evid = 1L, amt = wt * 1 / 2, ii = 12, addl = 27L,
    cmt = "depot"
  )
  # Observation on the ODE state `central`; Cc is returned alongside it.
  obs <- tibble::tibble(
    id = ids, time = 27 * 12 + 11.5, evid = 0L, amt = NA_real_, ii = 0,
    addl = 0L, cmt = "central"
  )
  dplyr::bind_rows(dose, obs) |>
    dplyr::mutate(WT = wt, etalcl = eta[match(id, ids)])
}

events <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(weights)), function(i) {
  make_events(weights$WT[i], i, z_grid * omega_sd)
})) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))

stopifnot(dplyr::n_distinct(events$id) == nrow(weights) * n_lattice)
```

```{r simulate}
solve_troughs <- function(ev) {
  rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = ev, omega = NA, returnType = "data.frame") |>
    dplyr::filter(time == 27 * 12 + 11.5) |>
    dplyr::select(id, WT, cl, trough_per_mgkgday = Cc)
}
tr1 <- suppressWarnings(solve_troughs(events))
stopifnot(nrow(tr1) == nrow(weights) * n_lattice, !anyNA(tr1$trough_per_mgkgday))

troughs <- tidyr::expand_grid(tr1, dose = doses) |>
  dplyr::mutate(Cc = trough_per_mgkgday * dose) |>
  dplyr::left_join(weights, by = "WT")
```

# Check 1 -- target attainment (Figures 5 and 7)

The paper's primary endpoint is the probability that the steady-state trough
lies in the 4-10 ng/mL target window, plotted against weight for each dose in
Figure 5 (adults) and Figure 7 (children). The published probabilities below
were read from those figures by the maintainers (precision about 1 percentage
point); the paper simulated 1,000 patients per scenario, so its own Monte Carlo
error is about 1.5 percentage points.

```{r published-pta}
# Rows: dose (mg/kg/day); columns: body weight (kg). Read from Figures 5 and 7.
fig5 <- rbind(
  `0.01` = c(0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0),
  `0.02` = c(7.5, 11.5, 16.0, 20.5, 25.5, 29.0),
  `0.04` = c(72.5, 79.0, 83.0, 83.5, 84.3, 83.7),
  `0.06` = c(76.0, 70.5, 65.0, 60.0, 53.3, 48.7),
  `0.08` = c(51.2, 41.4, 33.3, 26.0, 20.7, 16.5),
  `0.1` = c(26.5, 19.0, 13.5, 10.6, 8.1, 6.2),
  `0.12` = c(13.2, 9.4, 6.2, 5.0, 3.3, 2.0),
  `0.14` = c(7.3, 5.3, 3.0, 1.6, 0.6, 0.5)
)
colnames(fig5) <- c(50, 60, 70, 80, 90, 100)
fig7 <- rbind(
  `0.01` = c(0, 0, 0, 0),
  `0.02` = c(0, 0, 1.5, 3.6),
  `0.04` = c(5.8, 25.2, 45.0, 61.0),
  `0.06` = c(27.3, 62.1, 77.5, 78.7),
  `0.08` = c(49.7, 75.3, 70.8, 61.5),
  `0.1` = c(64.6, 68.0, 53.2, 38.7),
  `0.12` = c(69.8, 54.4, 35.3, 21.3),
  `0.14` = c(66.2, 42.4, 21.4, 12.3)
)
colnames(fig7) <- c(10, 20, 30, 40)

to_long <- function(m) {
  as.data.frame(as.table(m), stringsAsFactors = FALSE) |>
    dplyr::transmute(
      dose = as.numeric(Var1), WT = as.numeric(Var2), pta_published = Freq
    )
}
published <- dplyr::bind_rows(to_long(fig5), to_long(fig7))
```

```{r pta}
in_window <- function(c) mean(c >= 4 & c <= 10)

pta <- troughs |>
  dplyr::group_by(group, WT, dose) |>
  dplyr::summarise(pta_model = 100 * in_window(Cc), .groups = "drop") |>
  dplyr::left_join(published, by = c("WT", "dose")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(diff = pta_model - pta_published)

pta |>
  dplyr::select(group, dose, WT, pta_model) |>
  dplyr::mutate(dose = sprintf("%.2f", dose)) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = WT, values_from = pta_model) |>
  dplyr::rename("Population" = group, "Dose (mg/kg/day)" = dose) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Model probability (%) of a 4-10 ng/mL trough, by body weight (kg).")

knitr::kable(
  tibble::tibble(
    Statistic = c("Median abs. difference", "90th percentile abs. difference", "Max abs. difference"),
    `Percentage points` = c(
      stats::median(abs(pta$diff)),
      stats::quantile(abs(pta$diff), 0.9),
      max(abs(pta$diff))
    )
  ),
  digits = 1,
  caption = "Model vs published target attainment over all 80 dose-weight cells of Figures 5 and 7."
)
```

```{r pta-gate}
stopifnot(
  # Structural: a mis-transcribed CL/F, V/F, exponent or regimen moves the
  # curves by tens of points.
  stats::median(abs(pta$diff)) < 1.5,
  # Envelope: published values are digitised and carry Monte Carlo error.
  stats::quantile(abs(pta$diff), 0.9) < 3.5,
  max(abs(pta$diff)) < 5
)
```

```{r figure-5-7, fig.cap = "Replicates Figures 5 (adults) and 7 (children) of Cao 2026: probability of a 4-10 ng/mL steady-state trough. Lines: model; points: values read from the published figures."}
pta |>
  ggplot(aes(WT, pta_model, colour = factor(dose))) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(aes(y = pta_published), shape = 1) +
  facet_wrap(~group, scales = "free_x") +
  labs(
    x = "Body weight (kg)", y = "Probability of 4-10 ng/mL (%)",
    colour = "Dose (mg/kg/day)"
  )
```

The model reproduces both published figures across all 80 cells, including
the crossing points the paper used to define its weight bands (Table 4).

# Check 2 -- which quantities are on which scale

Table 3 prints `omega_CL/F = 0.172` and `sigma_1 = 2.504` without saying
whether either is a standard deviation or a variance, nor whether the
published Monte Carlo included residual error. The four combinations make
very different predictions, so they are compared against the published
attainment curves. Residual error is added analytically (additive normal
error), keeping the comparison deterministic.

```{r scale-check}
add_sd <- ui$theta[["addSd"]]

pta_variant <- function(omega_scale, resid_sd) {
  troughs |>
    dplyr::mutate(Cc_v = Cc * exp(z_grid[((id - 1L) %% n_lattice) + 1L] * (omega_scale - omega_sd))) |>
    dplyr::group_by(WT, dose) |>
    dplyr::summarise(
      pta = if (resid_sd == 0) {
        100 * in_window(Cc_v)
      } else {
        100 * mean(stats::pnorm((10 - Cc_v) / resid_sd) - stats::pnorm((4 - Cc_v) / resid_sd))
      },
      .groups = "drop"
    ) |>
    dplyr::left_join(published, by = c("WT", "dose")) |>
    dplyr::summarise(
      median_abs = stats::median(abs(pta - pta_published)),
      max_abs = max(abs(pta - pta_published))
    )
}

variants <- tibble::tribble(
  ~reading, ~omega_scale, ~resid_sd,
  "omega SD, no residual error (packaged)", 0.172, 0,
  "omega SD, residual SD 2.504 included", 0.172, 2.504,
  "omega variance (SD 0.415), no residual error", sqrt(0.172), 0,
  "omega variance, residual variance (SD 1.58) included", sqrt(0.172), sqrt(2.504)
)
variants <- dplyr::bind_cols(
  variants,
  dplyr::bind_rows(Map(pta_variant, variants$omega_scale, variants$resid_sd))
)

variants |>
  dplyr::select(reading, median_abs, max_abs) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Reading" = reading, "Median abs. difference (points)" = median_abs,
    "Max abs. difference (points)" = max_abs
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Agreement with Figures 5 and 7 under each reading of Table 3.")

stopifnot(
  variants$median_abs[1] < 2,
  all(variants$median_abs[-1] > 3 * variants$median_abs[1])
)
```

Only the packaged reading -- `omega_CL/F` a standard deviation and the
published probabilities computed on individual predictions without residual
error -- reproduces the paper. Reading the omega as a variance flattens every
curve (no dose reaches the published 75-85% peaks), and adding a 2.5 ng/mL
residual SD to a 4-10 ng/mL window pulls the peaks down by about 20 points.
Note that this check settles the omega scale only: the residual error is
absent from the paper's simulations, so the figures say nothing about whether
`sigma_1` is an SD or a variance. It is packaged as an SD, the convention the
same group's Table 3 format follows (compare `Wang_2019b_tacrolimus`).

# Check 3 -- Table 4 recommended doses

```{r table4}
table4 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~group, ~band, ~lo, ~hi, ~dose, ~published,
  "Adult", "[50-53)", 50, 53, 0.06, "74.5-76.0",
  "Adult", "[53-100]", 53, 100, 0.04, "74.5-84.3",
  "Child", "[10-12.7)", 10, 12.7, 0.12, "66.0-69.8",
  "Child", "[12.7-16.4)", 12.7, 16.4, 0.10, "66.0-68.0",
  "Child", "[16.4-26.7)", 16.4, 26.7, 0.08, "68.0-76.5",
  "Child", "[26.7-40]", 26.7, 40, 0.06, "74.0-78.7"
)

# The simulated weights that fall inside each band.
t4 <- table4 |>
  dplyr::rowwise() |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    pta_at_sim_wts = {
      p <- pta$pta_model[pta$group == group & pta$dose == dose & pta$WT >= lo & pta$WT <= hi]
      if (length(p) == 0) "none simulated" else paste(sprintf("%.1f", p), collapse = ", ")
    }
  ) |>
  dplyr::ungroup()

t4 |>
  dplyr::select(group, band, dose, published, pta_at_sim_wts) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Population" = group, "Weight band (kg)" = band, "Dose (mg/kg/day)" = dose,
    "Published attainment (%)" = published,
    "Model at simulated weights in band (%)" = pta_at_sim_wts
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Table 4 recommended doses. The band edges are interpolated crossing points, so only the simulated weights inside each band can be compared.")
```

The 12.7-16.4 kg band contains no simulated weight; its published range comes
from interpolating the curves at the band edges.

```{r figure-4, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 4 of Cao 2026: simulated steady-state troughs in adults by dose and weight. Dashed lines: 4-10 ng/mL target."}
troughs |>
  dplyr::filter(group == "Adult") |>
  ggplot(aes(factor(dose), Cc)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.size = 0.4) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(4, 10), linetype = "dashed", colour = "red") +
  facet_wrap(~ paste(WT, "kg"), ncol = 3) +
  labs(x = "Daily dose (mg/kg/day, in two doses)", y = "Trough (ng/mL)")
```

# PKNCA validation

The paper reports no non-compartmental analysis, so `ncaComparisonTable()` is
not used. Instead PKNCA is run on a single 5 mg oral dose to a 70 kg lattice
and compared with the model's closed-form solution. Both sides use the same
parameters, so the difference is purely numerical and the bound is tight.

```{r pknca}
nca_times <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 3, by = 0.02), seq(3.25, 72, by = 0.25))))
nca_events <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  tibble::tibble(
    id = seq_len(n_lattice), time = 0, evid = 1L, amt = 5, cmt = "depot"
  ),
  tidyr::expand_grid(id = seq_len(n_lattice), time = nca_times) |>
    dplyr::mutate(evid = 0L, amt = NA_real_, cmt = "central")
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(WT = 70, etalcl = z_grid[id] * omega_sd, treatment = "5 mg single oral dose") |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))

nca_sim <- suppressWarnings(rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod,
  events = nca_events, omega = NA, returnType = "data.frame",
  keep = "treatment"
))

sim_nca <- nca_sim |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, Cc, treatment)
sim_nca <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  sim_nca,
  sim_nca |> dplyr::distinct(id, treatment) |> dplyr::mutate(time = 0, Cc = 0)
) |>
  dplyr::distinct(id, treatment, time, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, time)

dose_df <- nca_events |>
  dplyr::filter(evid == 1L) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, amt, treatment)

nca_data <- PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(sim_nca, Cc ~ time | treatment + id),
  PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | treatment + id),
  intervals = data.frame(
    start = 0, end = Inf, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE,
    aucinf.obs = TRUE, half.life = TRUE
  )
)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(nca_data)
summary(nca_res)
```

```{r pknca-vs-closed-form}
closed_form <- nca_sim |>
  dplyr::distinct(id, cl, vc, ka) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    kel = cl / vc,
    aucinf_cf = 1000 * 5 / cl,
    halflife_cf = log(2) / kel,
    tmax_cf = log(ka / kel) / (ka - kel)
  )

cmp <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("aucinf.obs", "half.life", "tmax")) |>
  dplyr::select(id, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES) |>
  dplyr::mutate(id = as.integer(as.character(id))) |>
  dplyr::left_join(closed_form, by = "id") |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    auc_pct = 100 * (aucinf.obs - aucinf_cf) / aucinf_cf,
    hl_pct = 100 * (half.life - halflife_cf) / halflife_cf,
    tmax_pct = 100 * (tmax - tmax_cf) / tmax_cf
  )

knitr::kable(
  tibble::tibble(
    Parameter = c("AUC0-inf vs Dose/(CL/F)", "Half-life vs ln(2)/kel", "Tmax vs ln(ka/kel)/(ka-kel)"),
    `Median % difference` = c(stats::median(cmp$auc_pct), stats::median(cmp$hl_pct), stats::median(cmp$tmax_pct)),
    `Max abs % difference` = c(max(abs(cmp$auc_pct)), max(abs(cmp$hl_pct)), max(abs(cmp$tmax_pct)))
  ),
  digits = 3,
  caption = "PKNCA on the simulation vs the model's own closed-form solution."
)

# Same parameters on both sides: differences are numerical only. Tmax is
# resolved to half a 0.02 h grid step (~1.5% of the ~0.7 h Tmax).
stopifnot(
  max(abs(cmp$auc_pct)) < 1,
  max(abs(cmp$hl_pct)) < 1,
  max(abs(cmp$tmax_pct)) < 3
)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

- **`omega_CL/F = 0.172` is read as a standard deviation** (about 17% CV;
  see Check 2): the variance reading cannot reproduce Figures 5 and 7. The
  bootstrap median of 0.094 is well below the estimate (bias -45%), so this
  IIV is poorly determined in 31 patients; the packaged value is the final
  estimate, not the bootstrap median.
- **`sigma_1 = 2.504` is read as an additive SD in ng/mL.** The paper's
  dosing simulations do not use it, so nothing in the paper tests this
  reading; it follows the convention of the same group's earlier tacrolimus
  model (`Wang_2019b_tacrolimus`).
- **Published attainment excludes residual error.** The paper does not say
  so, but only the individual-prediction calculation reproduces its figures
  (Check 2).
- **Trough time.** Troughs are read 11.5 h after a dose, matching the
  "about 30 minutes before the next dose" sampling described in Methods.
- **Children are an extrapolation.** No child contributed data. The paper's
  paediatric doses (Figures 6-7, Table 4) apply the adult model with the
  fixed allometric exponents down to 10 kg, without a maturation function.
  The packaged model inherits that limitation.
- **Matrix.** The paper names the assay (Emit 2000 Tacrolimus, a whole-blood
  immunoassay) but not the matrix; the central compartment is recorded as
  whole blood on that basis.
- **Fixed `ka`.** 4.48 1/h is carried from the source's references 33-34
  (Wang 2020, two Xenobiotica tacrolimus analyses), as also used by
  `Wang_2019b_tacrolimus`.
- **Figure values were digitised by eye** from Figures 5 and 7 to about
  1 percentage point. The gate is set on the median and 90th percentile of the
  absolute differences, not on individual cells.
